name: image-colour-analyzer
description: Web tool for analyzing colour properties in large image datasets

paragraphs: A browser-based tool for measuring colour across a whole set of images at once. It clusters each image into its dominant colours, reports colour values in HSV, CIELAB and LCH, computes a suite of whole-image and spatial metrics, reads EXIF (including GPS), and exports everything as CSV. It handles ordinary flat photos as well as 360° / wide-angle imagery (equirectangular, fisheye, and azimuthal / tiny-planet projections), with solid-angle weighting, projection conversion, and polar spatial analysis. The tool is subject-agnostic — axes are labelled generically in degrees, so it is not specific…
Part of Vis-O-Matic, alongside Image Cutter and Image Visualizer.
features: Batch colour analysis — drop in a folder or a list of URLs; each image is downsampled to an analysis resolution you set, then measured locally.
K-means clustering — k-means++ initialisation with a fixed seed for reproducibility; 2–20 dominant colours per image, each reported in HSV, CIELAB and LCH with its pixel share.
Three levels of granularity — cluster-level, image-level, and optional pixel-level tables, plus a hue histogram.
EXIF passthrough — GPS, capture date, camera and orientation read from JPEGs and from PNGs carrying an eXIf chunk, including cut-outs exported by Image Cutter with GPS/EXIF preserved.
Transparency handling — composite transparent areas onto white, black or grey, or analyse opaque pixels only.

requirements.text: Open the tool in a browser — no installation, no account, no server.
There is no server, no account and no upload step.
